issues_in: Spot-checked URL https://www.iid.com/about-iid/community/data-center-facts (cited in sources.refresh_2026_08_11 and in contradictions) returns HTTP 403 for both curl and the browse
fixed: Retried the flagged URL once: HEAD and GET both returned HTTP 403 (confirmed dead/bot-blocked).

Found verified replacement via Wayback Machine: same official IID page captured 2026-07-24 (https://web.archive.org/web/20260724093439/https://www.iid.com/about-iid/community/data-center-facts); fetched and confirmed archived text supports the cited facts (IID evaluates proposals for reliability, feasibility, cost recovery, interconnection/operational requirements, and will not expedite projects).

Replaced the dead URL in data.json sources.refresh_2026_08_11 (official_utility_context item) with the Wayback capture and documented the swap in the facts text (original live URL retained in prose for provenance).
Replaced the dead URL in data.json contradictions[0].sources with the Wayback capture.
Added a data.json history entry (date 2026-08-11, field sources) recording previous_value, new_value, and change_reason for the swap.
Added a dated URL-fix note to NOTES.md 2026-08-11 section with the replacement URL and verification details.
Validated data.json parses as valid JSON after all edits.
remaining_risks: IID's live data-center facts page returns HTTP 403 to automated access (likely bot protection); if it is reachable in a normal browser it may work for humans, but the Wayback capture is the dependable citation for automated use.
The original live URL is retained only in prose (facts text and history previous_value) for provenance, not as an active source URL.
summary: Fixed the single assigned issue for USDC-0088: the IID data-center facts URL (https://www.iid.com/about-iid/community/data-center-facts) returned HTTP 403 on retry (HEAD and GET), so it was replaced in sources.refresh_2026_08_11 and contradictions[0].sources with a verified Wayback Machine capture of the same official page (snapshot 2026-07-24) whose archived text confirms the cited facts. A history entry and a NOTES.md dated note document the swap, and data.json remains valid JSON.
